questions.question: How many times in a week does both the hands of the clock will coincide with each other?
questions.solution:
Both hands of Clock coincide with each other 22 times a day.

That is, angle between to hands will be 0o .

The hands Coincide with each other in every hour Except between (12 -1).

The Timings at Which hands coincide is,

AM : 12:00, 1:05, 2:11, 3:16,4:22, 5:27, 6:33, 7:38, 8:44, 9:49, 10:55.

PM: 12:00, 1:05, 2:11, 3:16, 4:22, 5:27, 6:33, 7:38, 8:44, 9:49, 10:55.

Total 22 times in a day.

**In 7 days = 7 × 22 = 154**

Hence, 154 is the correct answer.

questions.question: 11 January 2018 is a Thursday. On which day will 11 June 2019 fall?
questions.solution:
11 January 2018 = Thursday

As 2018 is not a leap year, 11 January 2019 = Friday

As 2019 is not a leap year, number of days from 11 January 2019 to 11 June 2019 = (20 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 11 = 151)

151/7 = 21 and 4 days

Hence on 11 June 2019, it will be Friday + 4 days = Tuesday.

questions.question: When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun moves in the opposite direction. This illustrates Newton’s:

options.text: First and second law of motion

questions.solution:
__
 
• **Newton’s third law of motion:__** Every action force has an equal and opposite reaction force that acts simultaneously.
 
• According to the above law, the forward-moving bullet causes the gun to move backward after firing. This backward motion of the gun is called its recoil.
 
• **Newton First law** states that Every object remains in uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change its state by the action of an external force.
 
• **Newton's Second Law of motion** states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied force in the direction of the force. i.e. F=ma. Where F is the force applied, m is the mass of the body, and a is the acceleration produced.

questions.question: The average of three numbers is 6. The average of the first two is 5 while the average of the last two is 8. The three numbers are:
questions.solution:
Let the three numbers be a, b and c.

Given average of three numbers = 6

⇒ (a + b + c)/3 = 6

⇒ a + b + c = 18 ----(1)

Given average of the first two number = 5

⇒ (a + b)/2 = 5

⇒ a + b = 10 ----(2)

Given average of the last two numbers = 8

⇒ (b + c)/2 = 8

⇒ b + c = 16 ----(3)

From equation (1) & (2)

⇒ c = 8

⇒ b + c = 16

⇒ b = 16 – 8 = 8

∴ The numbers are 2, 8 and 8.

questions.question: If the zeroes of polynomial x² – ax + b are 3 and 4, then ‘a’ and ‘b’ are respectively equal to
questions.solution:
Let f(x) = x² – ax + b

Given, 3 and 4 are zero of f(x),

f(3) = 0

⇒ 3² – 3a + b = 0

⇒ 9 – 3a + b = 0 ---- (1)

f(4) = 0

⇒ 4² – 4a + b = 0

⇒ 16 – 4a + b = 0 ----(2)

⇒ 9 – 3a + b = 16 – 4a + b

⇒ 9 – 3a = 16 – 4a

⇒ a = 7

Substitute a = 7 in equation

⇒ 9 – 21 + b = 0

⇒ b = 12

∴ a = 7, b = 12

questions.question:
Arrange the following in a proper sequence.

A Mutation

B Reproductive isolation

C Natural selection

D Evolution
questions.solution:
Correct order is as follows:

Mutation → Reproductive isolation → Natural selection → Evolution

Mutation is a change that occur in DNA sequence.

Reproductive isolation refers to inability of related species to breed.

Natural selection is a consistent difference in survival and reproduction between different genes.

Evolution is the change in the characteristics of a species over several generations and relies on the process of natural selection.

Thus, the correct order is A, B, C, D.

questions.question: Peter belongs to Town A and Paul belongs to Town B. They start their journeys towards each other’s towns following the same route at the same time. They meet somewhere on the way and continue with their journeys. After meeting Paul, Peter takes another 13.5 hours to reach his destination while Paul takes another 6 hours to reach Peter’s town. If Peter travelled at the speed of 30 km/h, what was Paul’s speed in km/h?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5e751e457a44a5112d54dac85e36846729e4b52ed03a9a5bb208abb95a3664c.png] 

At x hours later and Paul meet each other.

Distance (d) = (Relative speed) × time

Given that the speed of Peter = 30 km/hr

Let speed of Paul = y km/hr

Let the distance between Town A and Town B be d

⇒ d = (30 + y) × x ----(1)

Given that Paul takes another 6 hours after meeting peter to reach town B.

⇒ d = y(x + 6) ----(2)

Similarly, Peter takes another 13.5 hours after.

Meeting Paul to reach town A.

⇒ d = 30(x + 13.5) ----(3)

From equation (1) & (2)

⇒ (30 + y)x = y(x + 6)

⇒ 30x + xy = xy + 6y

⇒ 30x = 6y

⇒ y = 5x

From equations (1) & (3)

⇒ (30 + y)x = 30(x + 13.5)

⇒ 30x + xy = 30x + 30 × 13.5

⇒ xy = 30 × 27/2

⇒ xy = 15 × 27

⇒ x² = 81

⇒ x = 9

⇒ y = 5 × 9 = 45 km/hr

∴ Speed of Paul = 45 km/h

questions.solution:

questions.question:
Consider the given question and decide which of the following statement is sufficient to answer the question.

What is X’s rank from the top in a class of 50 students?

**Statements: **

1. Y’s rank is 4 ranks below that of X and 30th from the bottom.

2. Z’s rank is 2 ranks above that of X and 32ⁿd from the bottom.

options.text: 2 alone is sufficient while 1 alone is not sufficient to answer the given question.
Either 1 or 2 is sufficient to answer the given question.
Both 1 and 2 are sufficient to answer the given question.
1 alone is sufficient while 2 alone is not sufficient to answer the given question.

questions.solution:
**From statement 1: **Y’s rank is 4 ranks below that of X and 30th from the bottom.

Thus X’s rank is 34th from the bottom.

As the total number of students is 50, X’s rank from the top will be 50 – 34 + 1 = 17

**From statement 2: **Z’s rank is 2 ranks above that of X and 32ⁿd from the bottom.

Thus, X’s rank is 30th from the bottom.

As the total number of students is 50, X’s rank from the top will be 50 – 30 + 1 = 21

So, we can say that either 1 or 2 is sufficient to answer the given question.

questions.question: If the velocity of a body becomes two times its initial velocity, its kinetic energy becomes n times its initial kinetic energy. What is the value of n?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option **2**, i.e __**4**__.

__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Kinetic energy (KE): The energy possessed by a body by virtue of its motion is called kinetic energy.

KE = (1)/(2)m{v²}

Where m = mass of the body and v = velocity of the body

**CALCULATION**__:

Let the initial velocity be u and final velocity be v.

According to the given question, velocity becomes two times its initial velocity. This means V = 2u

**Initial kinetic energy (KE)** = 1/2 mu²

**Final kinetic energy (KE')** =1/2 mv² =1/2 m(2u)² =1/2 m × 4u² =4 × **1/2 mu²**

**KE' = 4 × KE, where n = 4**

∴ The Kinetic energy becomes **4 times** when **velocity is doubled.**

questions.question: An incident ray strikes a plane mirror at an angle of 20° with the mirror. The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is ________.
questions.solution:
**__Laws of reflection:__**

1. The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

2. The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal lie in the same plane.

3. The reflected ray and the incident ray are on opposite sides of the normal.

__
 
• Angle of reflection = ∠r
 
• Angle of incidence = ∠i
 
• The angle between the plane mirror and incident ray = 20°

According Law of reflection:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba310ec8a33b6876833335a27b7097d2a4c6dd55c6f634934519a02c7c8ffb23.png] 

 
• 20° + ∠r + ∠i + 20° = 180°
 
• ∠r + ∠i = 140°
 
• The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is **140°.__**

options.text: Its Potential and Kinetic energies decrease

There is no change in its Potential or Kinetic energy
Its Potential energy decreases while its Kinetic energy increase

questions.solution:
__
 
• **Kinetic energy:__** The energy an object has because of its motion is called its kinetic energy.

**K. E. = 1/2mv²**

__
 
• **Potential energy:__** The energy stored in an object because of its specific state or position is called its potential energy.

**P.E. = mgh**

 
• Every object has potential energy when it is at a height above the ground and it keeps getting converted to kinetic energy as the object falls towards the ground.

questions.solution:
__
 
• Turtle - Reptiles
 
• Crocodile - Reptiles
 
• **Toad - Amphibia**__
 
• Snake - Reptiles

__**Concept:**__

**Reptiles**

__
 
• Reptiles are cold-blooded animals that raise their body temperature by lying in the sun or lowering it by crawling into the shade. 
 
• Their body temperature changes to the temperature of their surroundings. Because of this, snakes that live in colder climates must hibernate through the winter.
 
• There are more than 2,900 species of snakes in the world. 

Amphibians

 
• Amphibians are organisms that live a dual life. They can live on land as well as in water.
 
• They have porous skin that requires moisture. Also, amphibians lay eggs in the water, and their young have gills to survive in the water.
 
• They venture onto land only when fully mature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Characteristics of Reptilia

__
 
• Following are the important characteristics of the animals belonging to Class Reptilia:

 
 
• These are creeping and burrowing terrestrial animals with scales on their body.
 
• They are cold-blooded animals found in most of the warmer regions of the world.
 
• Their skin is dry, and rough, without any glands.
 
• The body is divided into head, neck, trunk, and tail.
 
• Few of these shed the scales on their skin as skin cast.
 
• The respiration takes place with the help of the lungs.
 
• The skull is Monocondylic.
 
• They have two pairs of pentadactyl limbs, each bearing claws. Snakes are an exception.
 
• The heart is 3 chambered. However, crocodiles have a 4-chambered heart.
 
• The nervous system comprises 12 pairs of cranial nerves.
 
• The lateral line system is absent in reptiles.
 
• Except for snakes, all the reptiles have well-developed ears.
 
• They possess a typical cloaca.

Absent
